newsitem.title: UK: Export demand for UK goods lowest since 1993 - CBI.
newsitem.headline: Export demand for UK goods lowest since 1993 - CBI.

text.p: Export demand for British manufactured goods has reached its lowest level since November 1993 because of the strong pound, the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) said.

But its March monthly trends survey showed manufacturers reported improved overall demand, with a negative balance of one percent saying total order books were below normal compared with a negative balance of six percent in February.
"This month's result, with the exception of last November, is the first time that total order books have been reported as close to normal since September 1995," the CBI said.
The survey showed 35 percent of manufacturing firms regarded export order books as below normal while 17 percent said they were above normal, a negative balance of 18 percent.

"These results show that the strength of sterling is beginning to take its toll on export orders, which are at their weakest level since November 1993," said Sudhir Junankar, the CBI's associate director of economic analysis.
"However, an improvement in domestic demand has more than compensated for the fall in exports and manufacturers have become more confident about raising output in the coming months."
The survey showed manufacturers expect output to increase markedly over the next four months and to a much greater extent than recorded in February.
A positive balance of 25 percent of firms expect output to increase, the most positive result since May 1995.
A positive balance of nine percent of firms expect domestic prices to rise over the next four months compared with a positive balance of four percent in February.
Stocks of finished goods remained more than adequate to meet expected demand.
A positive balance of 15 percent of firms said they had more than adequate stocks compared with 14 percent in February.
The CBI said 1,077 firms, representing 50 industries and accounting for around half of manufacturing exports and some two million employees, responded to the survey between February 21 and March 12.
